common_confusions: BC-MIS-08002 (the definite integral itself read as the average)
BC-SKL-08004 (average of the values confused with average rate of change)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (the interval has length other than one, so the division is visible in the answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response writes the quotient with the definite integral of f over [a,b] above and b minus a below, evaluates it by antidifferentiation with endpoint substitution, and reports a number carrying the units of f; the limits and the divisor both come from the interval the prompt names, and neither BC-ERR-08001 nor BC-ERR-08002 appears when the function arrives as a model formula and when it arrives as a graph.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of f over the stated interval is correct and its value is handed in as the average with no quotient anywhere, which is BC-ERR-08001 and the observation recorded in BC-SIG-08001; or the averaging structure is right while the limits and the divisor are read off an interval the prompt did not name, which is BC-ERR-08002.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative of f is wrong or the endpoint substitution is mishandled before any averaging takes place, which is an evaluation gap at BC-SKL-06034 rather than an average value gap; a model whose function notation is misread, so that f(a) and a itself are interchanged, is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08002 (that the integral accumulates the function and the division converts the accumulation to a mean) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating the definite integral itself) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given f by an analytic expression and an interval [a,b], compute the definite integral of f over [a,b] and divide by b minus a.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the function over the interval and divide by the length of the interval.
skills.name: Apply the average value formula to a function given by a formula

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08002 (the definite integral itself read as the average)
BC-MIS-06011 (integral read as area regardless of sign)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (the graph dips below the axis, so sign and division are separable in the same answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: Signed area is read off the segments and circular arcs of the given graph, regions below the horizontal axis entering the total negatively, and that value is then divided by the length of the interval; the semicircle contributions use the correct radius and the reported average is stated as a function value, with BC-ERR-08001 and BC-ERR-08003 both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: All the geometric pieces are computed correctly and the integral value is reported as the average, the division by the interval length never appearing, which is BC-ERR-08001; or a portion of the graph below the axis is counted as a positive contribution, which is BC-ERR-08003 and leaves the quotient structure intact while the number is too large.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The area of a trapezoid, triangle, or semicircle on the figure is itself wrong, which is BC-PRQ-06007 rather than an averaging gap; reading area from a graph at all, including the sign convention, sits at BC-SKL-06028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08002 (the division that turns accumulated signed area into a mean value) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06028 (signed area from a piecewise linear and circular graph) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given the graph of f made of segments and circular arcs, evaluate the definite integral of f as signed area and divide by the length of the interval.
skills.description_plain: Get the area under the graph by geometry, then divide by the width of the interval.
skills.name: Compute an average value from a graph using geometry

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
BC-MIS-08009 (a reported result treated as complete once the number is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (the integrand has no elementary antiderivative, so the written setup is the only evidence of method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The page carries the integral expression with its limits and its differential, visible evidence of the division by the interval length, and a value reported to three places after the decimal point; stored values rather than truncated decimals feed the final computation, so neither BC-ERR-08004 nor BC-ERR-08005 is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal appears alone with no integral and no quotient written down, which is BC-ERR-08004; or the setup is complete and an intermediate decimal is truncated to two or three places before the last step, moving the reported value, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The answer is correct but given to one place, or rounded rather than truncated against the convention, which is a reporting gap at BC-PRQ-08006 rather than a failure of the average value setup itself.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08003 (that the written expression, not the calculator display, is the mathematical claim) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (three place reporting and storing unrounded intermediates) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Show the definite integral together with evidence of division by the length of the interval, then report the value accurate to three places after the decimal point.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral and the division before reporting the decimal the calculator gives.
skills.name: Present the calculator setup for an average value and report it

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08001 (average value and average rate of change treated as one quantity)
BC-MIS-08002 (the integral itself read as the average)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (asks for the mean of the values)
BC-QA-08002 (asks for an average rate of change and then for the instant matching it, so the two quantities appear in one question)
adaptive.mastered_if: Given a prompt, the response selects the integral quotient when the mean of the function values is wanted and the difference quotient of the endpoint values when the average rate of change is wanted, and the units attached to the answer are the units of f in the first case and units of f per unit of the input in the second; BC-ERR-08006 does not appear in either direction.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: One of the two quantities is built correctly and the other is answered with the first, which is BC-ERR-08006; the specific pattern in BC-SIG-08002 is the change in the function over the change in the input reported under the name average value.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Net change over the interval cannot be formed at all, so neither quotient can be assembled, which is BC-SKL-06036 rather than a discrimination gap; misreading which symbol in the prompt names the function is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08001 (that one averages function values and the other averages a rate) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06036 (forming net change over an interval) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a prompt, select the integral quotient when the average of the function values is wanted and the difference quotient when the average rate of change is wanted.
skills.description_plain: Decide which of the two averages a question is asking for before computing.
skills.name: Distinguish average value from average rate of change

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08001 (average value and average rate of change treated as one quantity)
BC-SKL-08015 (interpreting an accumulation integral rather than an average)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08001 (requires the average reported in context)
BC-QA-08007 (a displayed integral must be described with quantity, interval, and units)
adaptive.mastered_if: A sentence names the quantity being averaged, the interval over which the average is taken, and units that are the units of the integrand rather than rate units; when the reported figure is an average rate of change the units are per unit of input, and BC-ERR-08007 and BC-ERR-08006 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The value and the quantity are named while the units are left off or assembled from the wrong factors, which is BC-ERR-08007; or the sentence is well formed but describes the other average, which is BC-ERR-08006.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The sentence cannot name what f measures because the function notation in the context has not been decoded, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an interpretation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08001 (which of the two averages carries rate units) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08007 (building units from the factors already in the integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Report an average value as a quantity in the units of the integrand, naming the quantity and the interval over which the average is taken.
skills.description_plain: Say what the average stands for in the situation and attach its units.
skills.name: State the meaning and units of an average value in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-SKL-08007 (total distance, which needs the absolute value)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (velocity changes sign inside the interval, so displacement and distance separate numerically)
adaptive.mastered_if: Displacement is written as the definite integral of the velocity function itself, with no absolute value, over the time interval the prompt gives, and the reported value keeps its sign so that a negative answer is described as net movement in the negative direction; the integrand is not altered when the velocity changes sign on the interval, and BC-ERR-08008 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of velocity is set up and evaluated correctly and the value is then labelled as the distance travelled, which is BC-ERR-08008 and the observation in BC-SIG-08003; the setup for displacement stands while the naming of the quantity does not.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Net change of a quantity from its rate cannot be assembled at all, so the integral never reaches velocity, which is BC-SKL-06036; failing to read v(t) as the rate that goes inside the integral is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08004 (that the sign of velocity subtracts from displacement and not from distance) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06036 (net change as the integral of a rate) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function and a time interval, write and evaluate the definite integral of velocity over that interval and report it as displacement.
skills.description_plain: Integrate velocity over the interval to get the net change in position.
skills.name: Compute displacement as the definite integral of velocity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-MIS-08005 (speed treated as another name for velocity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (both displacement and total distance are asked in the same question, isolating the integrand choice)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integrand is the absolute value of the velocity function, the limits are the time interval stated, and the value returned is nonnegative and named as total distance travelled; the absolute value bars are written in the expression rather than applied to the answer, and neither BC-ERR-08008 nor BC-ERR-08009 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is written over the right interval with velocity itself as the integrand and the result called distance, which is BC-ERR-08008 with BC-SIG-08003 as its observed form; or the word speed is used while the expression keeps the signed velocity, which is BC-ERR-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value of a sign changing expression cannot be unpacked piecewise, so the integrand is never formed, which is BC-PRQ-08003 rather than a distance gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08005 (speed as the magnitude of velocity) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08003 (absolute value as a piecewise definition inside an integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a velocity function and a time interval, write and evaluate the definite integral of the absolute value of velocity over that interval and report it as total distance travelled.
skills.description_plain: Integrate the absolute value of velocity over the interval.
skills.name: Compute total distance as the definite integral of speed

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-SKL-08006 (displacement, which needs no splitting)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (velocity has an interior zero with a sign change, so the split is what separates the two totals)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation velocity equal to zero is solved on the interval, the resulting times are used to cut the interval into subintervals, velocity is integrated on each piece, and the absolute values of those pieces are summed; the answer exceeds the absolute displacement whenever a sign change occurs, and BC-ERR-08010 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The sign change is acknowledged in words while one integral is taken over the whole interval with a single absolute value at the end, which is BC-ERR-08010 and returns a total that is too small by twice the negative lobe.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation velocity equal to zero is not solved correctly, so the cut points are wrong before any integration, which is BC-PRQ-08001; not rewriting the absolute value piecewise on each subinterval is BC-PRQ-08003.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08004 (why the negative lobe adds to distance) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (solving for the times where velocity vanishes) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Solve velocity equal to zero on the interval, integrate velocity on each subinterval, and sum the absolute values of the results to obtain total distance.
skills.description_plain: Break the interval where the velocity crosses zero, then add the pieces without their signs.
skills.name: Split a time interval at the sign changes of velocity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08006 (displacement, which is the integral alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (a position value is requested from an initial condition)
BC-QA-08004 (the same structure with a contextual rate rather than a velocity)
adaptive.mastered_if: Position at time b is written as the given position at time a plus the definite integral of velocity from a to b, the initial value appearing as an explicit term in the expression rather than only in words, and the reported coordinate changes when the initial position changes; BC-ERR-08011 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The definite integral of velocity between the two times is evaluated correctly and reported as the position, the known value at the earlier time never entering the expression, which is BC-ERR-08011 and the state observed in BC-SIG-08004.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The pattern initial value plus accumulated change is not available in the simpler unit 6 setting either, which is BC-SKL-06037 rather than a motion gap; reading which symbol carries the initial position is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (that the integral gives change and not the amount) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (assembling final value from initial value and accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given an initial position at time a and a velocity function, evaluate the position at time b as the initial position plus the definite integral of velocity from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Add the accumulated change to the starting position.
skills.name: Determine a position value from an initial position and velocity

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08009 (the same structure one level up, position from velocity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (acceleration is given and a velocity at a later time is requested)
adaptive.mastered_if: Velocity at time b is expressed as the given velocity at time a plus the definite integral of acceleration from a to b, with the initial velocity present as a term and the limits running from the time of the known value to the time requested; the reported velocity keeps its sign, and BC-ERR-08011 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of acceleration is computed correctly and reported as the velocity, the known velocity at the earlier time left out of the expression, which is BC-ERR-08011 applied one derivative level down from position.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The initial value plus accumulation structure is itself missing, which is BC-SKL-06037; confusing a(t) with v(t) in the prompt, so the wrong function is integrated, is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (accumulated acceleration as change in velocity) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (adding the initial value to an accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given an initial velocity at time a and an acceleration function, evaluate the velocity at time b as the initial velocity plus the definite integral of acceleration from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Add the accumulated change in velocity to the starting velocity.
skills.name: Determine a velocity value from an initial velocity and acceleration

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08004 (distance travelled and net change in position treated as one quantity)
BC-MIS-08005 (speed treated as another name for velocity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08003 (the wording alone decides the integrand, with no computation to hide behind)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response classifies the requested quantity from the wording, saying that displacement or net change in position calls for the integral of velocity and that total distance travelled calls for the integral of the absolute value of velocity, and it names the integrand each choice requires before any computation; BC-ERR-08008 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The two quantities are described in words but the same integrand is named for both, which is BC-ERR-08008 in its classification form and matches BC-SIG-08003, where one value is offered for both questions in the same part.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The phrase net change cannot be tied to the function notation in the stem at all, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a discrimination gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08004 (the distinction the two words carry) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08007 (writing the absolute value integrand once the classification is made) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a motion prompt, classify the requested quantity as displacement or as total distance travelled and name the integrand each one requires.
skills.description_plain: Read whether the question wants net change in position or the length of the trip.
skills.name: Select displacement or total distance from the wording of a prompt

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
BC-SKL-08016 (writing the integral expression alone, without the initial amount)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (a known amount at one time and a modelled rate, so the initial term is the scored difference)
adaptive.mastered_if: The amount at time b is written as the given amount at time a plus the definite integral of the rate from a to b, with the differential and both limits present, and the number reported answers how much is present rather than how much it changed; neither BC-ERR-08011 nor BC-ERR-08012 appears, and the value moves when the initial amount is changed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The accumulation integral is correct and is reported without the initial amount, which is BC-ERR-08011 and the state in BC-SIG-08004; or the net change is computed and offered as the answer to a question asking what is present at that time, which is BC-ERR-08012.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The initial value plus accumulated change form is not reproduced even for a simple rate, which is BC-SKL-06037; a rate function misread as the amount itself in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08006 (the integral as change in the quantity) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06037 (assembling the total from initial value and accumulation) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given an initial amount at time a and a rate function, write and evaluate the amount at time b as the initial amount plus the definite integral of the rate from a to b.
skills.description_plain: Write the later amount as the starting amount plus the integral of the rate.
skills.name: Express the amount at a time as an initial amount plus an integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08007 (two rates acting at once combined by addition)
BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08005 (a rate in and a rate out act on one stored quantity, so the order of subtraction is visible in the sign)
adaptive.mastered_if: The net rate is written as the inflow rate minus the outflow rate, in that order, the difference enclosed in parentheses when it is placed inside an integral, and the net change over the interval is the definite integral of that difference; neither BC-ERR-08013 nor BC-ERR-08014 appears, and the sign of the result agrees with which rate is larger.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both rate functions are identified correctly and combined with a plus sign, or subtracted in the reverse order, which is BC-ERR-08013; or the difference is substituted into the integrand without parentheses so that only its first term is integrated or negated, which is BC-ERR-08014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Which of the two given functions is the inflow cannot be decided from the stem, so the difference is assembled from the wrong pair, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a net rate gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08007 (that the two rates move the stored amount in opposite directions) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08014 (parenthesising a substituted difference) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given separate inflow and outflow rate functions, write the net rate as their difference and express the net change over an interval as the definite integral of that difference.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the outflow rate from the inflow rate before integrating.
skills.name: Set up a net rate as rate in minus rate out

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08008 (a local extremum argument taken to settle an absolute extremum)
BC-SKL-05020 (classifying an interior critical point, which is the local question)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08006 (the amount is defined by an integral on a closed interval, so an endpoint can carry the maximum)
adaptive.mastered_if: The net rate is set equal to zero and solved on the interval, the interior candidates are listed together with both endpoints, and the maximum is settled either by a table of the amount at every candidate or by a stated sign change of the net rate from positive to negative with the uniqueness of that change asserted; BC-ERR-08015 and BC-ERR-08016 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The critical time is found correctly and the justification is a first or second derivative test presented as settling an absolute maximum, which is BC-ERR-08015; or a candidates table is built that contains only the interior critical time, which is BC-ERR-08016, the sign chart without endpoint comparison recorded in BC-SIG-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation net rate equal to zero is solved incorrectly, so the candidate list is wrong before any justification, which is BC-PRQ-08001; classifying a critical point from a sign change at all is BC-SKL-05020, and writing a justification that covers every candidate is BC-SKL-05028.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08008 (why an interval maximum needs the endpoints) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-05028 (writing the global justification) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Set the net rate equal to zero, identify the candidate times together with the endpoints, and justify the absolute maximum either by a sign change of the net rate with uniqueness or by evaluating the amount at every candidate.
skills.description_plain: Find where the net rate changes from positive to negative, then compare the candidates.
skills.name: Determine when an accumulated amount is maximal and justify globally

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08009 (an interpretation treated as complete once the quantity is named)
BC-MIS-08006 (the integral of a rate read as the amount of the quantity)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08007 (a displayed integral must be described, so quantity, interval, and units are the entire response)
adaptive.mastered_if: The sentence states the quantity that accumulates, the two times or inputs that bound the accumulation, and units that multiply the rate units by the input units; a signed integral is described as the change in the quantity over that span rather than as an amount present, and neither BC-ERR-08007 nor BC-ERR-08017 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The quantity and its units are correct while the interval is left out of the sentence, which is BC-ERR-08017 and the observation in BC-SIG-08006; or the sentence is complete except that units are missing or built only from the rate, which is BC-ERR-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: What the rate function measures in the context cannot be stated at all, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an interpretation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (that the sentence must fix quantity, interval, and units) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08007 (deriving units from the integrand and the differential) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of a contextual rate, state the accumulated quantity, the interval of accumulation, and the units of the result.
skills.description_plain: Say what the integral measures, over which interval, in which units.
skills.name: Interpret a definite integral of a rate in context with units

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08009 (an expression treated as complete once the quantity is named)
BC-SKL-08012 (the amount at a time, which adds the initial value to this integral)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (the requested net change must be written before it is evaluated)
BC-QA-08005 (the integrand is a difference of two rates, so its structure is visible in the expression)
adaptive.mastered_if: A single definite integral is produced whose value is the requested net change, carrying the rate as integrand, the two inputs from the context as limits, and the differential in the variable of the rate; the expression stands on its own without a stray equals sign to a number, and neither BC-ERR-08018 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand and the limits are right while the differential is missing, which is BC-ERR-08018; or the expression is complete in form and the limits are taken from inputs other than the ones the context bounds, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The rate in the stem cannot be separated from the amount, so the integrand is the wrong function, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (the integral expression as the object being scored) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08018 (attaching the differential and the correct limits) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given an applied description of a rate, produce a definite integral, with differential and limits, whose value is the requested net change.
skills.description_plain: Turn the sentence into an integral with the right integrand and limits.
skills.name: Write a definite integral expression that answers an applied question

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
BC-MIS-08009 (a result treated as complete once the number is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08004 (an applied amount must be both evaluated and reported in context)
adaptive.mastered_if: The integral is evaluated by an antiderivative or with technology and the number is reported in the context with the units of the accumulated quantity, to three places after the decimal point when technology is used; unrounded intermediates feed the final step, so neither BC-ERR-08005 nor BC-ERR-08007 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The evaluation is correct and the number is reported bare, without the units of the accumulated quantity, which is BC-ERR-08007; or an intermediate decimal is truncated before the last computation and the reported value moves in the third place, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The reported value carries the wrong number of decimal places or is rounded against the stated convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than an evaluation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08009 (what a reported accumulation must state) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (storing intermediates and reporting to three places) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the definite integral, by antidifferentiation or with technology, and report the result as the quantity the context asks for, at the required decimal accuracy.
skills.description_plain: Compute the integral, then answer the question in a sentence with units.
skills.name: Evaluate an applied accumulation integral and report it in context

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction in an area integrand treated as immaterial)
BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of the bounding curve alone)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (a shaded region between two graphs, where the order decides the sign of the result)
adaptive.mastered_if: One curve is named as the greater on the interval, supported either by evaluating both functions at an interior input and comparing the two values or by reading the figure, and that decision then fixes the order of subtraction in the integrand; BC-ERR-08020 does not follow, and the area reported from the resulting integral is positive.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both functions are evaluated correctly at the test input and the integrand is still written lower minus upper, so the integral value is negative, which is BC-ERR-08020 and the state observed in BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substituting the test input into the two expressions is itself done wrongly, so the comparison rests on wrong values, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an ordering gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08011 (why the order of subtraction is part of the claim and not a sign to repair later) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08019 (writing the integrand once the order is fixed) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given two functions and an interval, determine which function is greater on that interval by evaluating a test input or by reading the given figure.
skills.description_plain: Decide which graph is on top before writing the difference.
skills.name: Identify which curve is upper on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of one bounding curve)
BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction treated as immaterial)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the region is bounded above and below by curves rather than by the axis)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area integral is written with integrand the upper function minus the lower function, dx as the differential, and limits that are the x values bounding the region, the difference parenthesised so that the subtraction applies to the whole lower expression; neither BC-ERR-08020 nor BC-ERR-08018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The limits and the pair of functions are right while the difference is reversed, which is BC-ERR-08020; or the integrand and the limits are complete and no dx is written, which is BC-ERR-08018.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Area read from a graph as a definite integral is not available, so the difference of two curves has nothing to attach to, which is BC-SKL-06028; misreading which expression is f and which is g in the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08010 (that the second boundary is subtracted rather than ignored) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08018 (differential and limits on the written expression) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write a definite integral with integrand the difference of the two functions in the order upper minus lower, with the differential dx and the limits taken from the boundary.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of the top curve minus the bottom curve, dx.
skills.name: Set up the area integral of upper minus lower with respect to x

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than the boundary of the region)
BC-SKL-08021 (locating the same crossings with technology)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the region begins and ends at crossings rather than at stated endpoints)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two expressions are set equal, the equation is solved exactly by factoring, by the quadratic formula, or by an inverse operation, and the solutions that bound the shaded region are selected from the full solution set and used as the limits; extraneous roots outside the region are discarded with the selection stated, and BC-ERR-08019 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is solved correctly and the limits taken are the ends of the displayed domain or the axes of the picture rather than the intersection values, which is BC-ERR-08019 in its limit selection form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation formed by equating the two curves cannot be solved, so no candidate boundary values are produced, which is BC-PRQ-08001 rather than a limit selection gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08012 (what determines where the region begins and ends) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (solving the equation that locates the crossings) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Set the two functions equal, solve exactly for the inputs at which the graphs meet, and select the solutions that bound the region.
skills.description_plain: Solve the two expressions equal to each other by hand.
skills.name: Find intersection points algebraically to set the limits

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than the boundary of the region)
BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (the crossings are not exact values, so storing them is what protects the third decimal place)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation of the two curves is solved with technology on the stated domain, the solutions are stored rather than transcribed as short decimals, and the stored values are used as the limits of the area integral; the reported area agrees to three places with a recomputation from the stored limits, and neither BC-ERR-08005 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The crossings are located correctly and then written and reused as two or three place decimals, so the reported area differs in the third decimal place, which is BC-ERR-08005 and exactly the observation in BC-SIG-08008; or the solver is run over a window that returns a crossing outside the region, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The stored value is reported rounded to the wrong number of places or rounded rather than truncated, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than a solving gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08012 (which inputs bound the region) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (storing unrounded solutions before reusing them) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Use technology to solve the equation of the two functions on the stated domain, store the solutions, and use the stored values as limits of integration.
skills.description_plain: Use the solver or a graph to get the crossing inputs as decimals.
skills.name: Find intersection points with a calculator to set the limits

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction treated as immaterial)
BC-MIS-08010 (the area between curves read as the integral of one bounding curve)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08008 (a numerical area must be produced from the written integral)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area integral is evaluated either by an antiderivative with the limits substituted in the correct variable or with technology, and a nonnegative number is reported as the area; when a substitution is used the limits are converted to the new variable or the antiderivative is returned to the original one, and neither BC-ERR-08021 nor BC-ERR-08022 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The reversed difference is written and then set equal to the positive area, so a correct number sits under an incorrect equality, which is BC-ERR-08021; or an antiderivative found by substitution is evaluated at the original limits, which is BC-ERR-08022; the negative value reported without comment is BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative itself is wrong because a fractional or negative exponent is mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-06002; evaluating a definite integral by antidifferentiation and endpoint substitution at all is BC-SKL-06034.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08011 (why a negative value cannot be relabelled as the area) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-06034 (evaluating with correctly converted limits) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the area integral by an antiderivative or with technology and report a nonnegative value as the area of the region.
skills.description_plain: Antidifferentiate or use technology, then state the area.
skills.name: Evaluate an area integral and report the area

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08026 (choosing the variable of integration, a separate decision)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (the left and right boundaries are curves, so the rewrite in y is unavoidable)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation relating x and y is solved for x in terms of y, the branch chosen is the one that bounds the region, and the sign taken on a square root or the range chosen on an inverse is justified by a point on that boundary; the rewritten expression contains y and no x, so BC-ERR-08023 cannot arise downstream.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The equation is rearranged and the expression retained still contains x, or both branches of a square root are carried forward with no choice made, so an integrand in x is paired with dy, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the observation in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The algebra of isolating one variable, including taking a root or an inverse of both sides, does not go through, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a slicing gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (that the integrand must be written in the variable of the differential) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (solving the equation for x) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a curve described by an equation in x and y, solve for x as a function of y on the branch that bounds the region.
skills.description_plain: Solve the equation so that x is written in terms of y.
skills.name: Rewrite a curve as a function of y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08018 (the same comparison for upper and lower in x)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (horizontal slices, where right and left replace upper and lower)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both curves are expressed in y, a y value interior to the interval is substituted into each, and the curve returning the larger x is named as the right boundary; that decision then places the right expression first in the difference, and BC-ERR-08020 does not appear in the integrand that follows.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The comparison at the interior y is carried out correctly and the integrand is still written left minus right, giving a negative value that is reported or silently made positive, which is BC-ERR-08020 with the pattern recorded in BC-SIG-08007.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Substituting a y value into an expression written in y is itself mishandled, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than an ordering gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (which variable the comparison is made in) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08025 (placing the chosen order into the dy integral) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given two curves written in y and an interval of y values, determine which one gives the larger x value there.
skills.description_plain: Decide which graph is farther right before writing the difference.
skills.name: Identify which curve is to the right on an interval of y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window rather than a boundary)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (the region is bounded left and right, so both the limits and the integrand live in y)
adaptive.mastered_if: A definite integral in y is written with integrand the right curve minus the left curve, both expressions in y, dy as the differential, and limits that are the y values bounding the region, and it is then evaluated to a nonnegative number; neither BC-ERR-08024 nor BC-ERR-08018 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integrand is correct in y while the limits are the x values of the region, which is BC-ERR-08024; or the whole expression is right except the missing dy, which is BC-ERR-08018; an integrand still containing x under dy is the not mastered state in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary curves were never solved for x in terms of y, so nothing can be integrated with respect to y, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (matching integrand, limits, and differential to one variable) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (rewriting each boundary as a function of y) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write a definite integral in y with integrand the difference of the two curves in the order right minus left, with limits the y values bounding the region, and evaluate it.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of right minus left, dy, and evaluate it.
skills.name: Set up and evaluate an area integral with respect to y

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as a label for slicing direction)
BC-SKL-08023 (the rewrite itself, which the choice depends on)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08009 (horizontal slices keep one boundary throughout)
BC-QA-08008 (vertical slices do, so the two archetypes together isolate the choice)
adaptive.mastered_if: The region is examined for whether one function stays the upper boundary across the whole span of x or one stays the right boundary across the whole span of y, and the variable of integration is chosen so that a single difference serves throughout; the choice is stated along with the boundary that would change if the other variable were used, and BC-ERR-08023 does not follow.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The slicing direction is chosen correctly and the integrand is left in the other variable, so a function of x is paired with dy or the reverse, which is BC-ERR-08023 with the mismatch observed in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary equations cannot be rewritten in the other variable, so the choice is forced rather than made, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a decision gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (what fixes the variable of integration) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08023 (carrying out the rewrite the choice requires) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a region, decide whether vertical or horizontal slices keep one function as the upper or right boundary throughout, and select the variable of integration accordingly.
skills.description_plain: Pick the slicing direction that needs the fewest integrals.
skills.name: Choose whether to integrate in x or in y for a given region

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08014 (one integral treated as covering any region between two curves)
BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08010 (the curves exchange places inside the interval, so a missed crossing changes the answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The equation setting the two curves equal is solved across the whole interval, the count of solutions is checked against the figure or the sign of the difference, and the solutions are listed in increasing order to define the subintervals; an interior crossing between the outer two is found and used, so BC-ERR-08025 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The outer two crossings are found and used as a single pair of limits while an interior crossing goes unnoticed, which is BC-ERR-08025 and the single integral of a fixed difference recorded in BC-SIG-08010.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation has solutions the algebra does not produce, for example a root lost by dividing through by a common factor, which is BC-PRQ-08001 rather than a region decomposition gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08014 (that a crossing splits the region into pieces) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08001 (finding every solution of the equation) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Solve the equation of the two curves on the interval, verify that every solution has been found, and order the solutions to define the subintervals.
skills.description_plain: Find all the crossings in the interval and list them in order.
skills.name: Locate every intersection point and order them

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08011 (the order of subtraction treated as immaterial)
BC-MIS-08014 (one integral treated as covering the whole region)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08010 (the correct order differs between the two pieces of the same region)
adaptive.mastered_if: On each subinterval between consecutive crossings both functions are evaluated at an interior input, the greater one is named, and the order of subtraction is set separately for each piece so that every contribution is nonnegative; the order changes across a crossing, and BC-ERR-08020 is absent on every piece.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The subintervals are correct and one fixed order of subtraction is carried across all of them, so one piece integrates to a negative value, which is BC-ERR-08020 in its per piece form with BC-SIG-08007 as the observed negative result.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Evaluating the two expressions at the interior input is itself unreliable, so the comparison is wrong, which is BC-PRQ-06005 rather than a sign management gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08011 (why each piece needs its own order) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08029 (writing the pieces as a sum once the orders are fixed) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: On each subinterval between consecutive intersection points, evaluate both functions at an interior input to fix the order of subtraction.
skills.description_plain: Test each piece separately to see which curve is on top there.
skills.name: Determine which curve is greater on each subinterval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08014 (one integral treated as covering any region between two curves)
BC-SKL-08030 (the single absolute value integral, an alternative to the sum)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08010 (the region has two lobes, so a single signed integral undercounts it)
adaptive.mastered_if: The total area is written as a sum of definite integrals, one per subinterval, each with its own limits and with its integrand ordered so that the contribution is nonnegative; the limits of consecutive integrals meet at the crossings, and BC-ERR-08026 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The crossings are identified and a single integral of a fixed difference is written across them, so the lobes cancel and the reported area is too small, which is BC-ERR-08026 and the observation in BC-SIG-08010.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The crossing values that would serve as the shared limits were never produced, which is BC-SKL-08027; reading which expression belongs where in the sum is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08014 (that the region has pieces) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08028 (fixing the order on each piece before summing) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Express the total area as the sum of definite integrals, one over each subinterval, with the integrand written so that each contribution is nonnegative.
skills.description_plain: Add one integral per piece, each with its own order of subtraction.
skills.name: Write the area as a sum of definite integrals over the subintervals

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08014 (one integral treated as covering any region between two curves)
BC-SKL-08029 (the sum of integrals, the other correct form)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08010 (technology is available, so the absolute value integrand is a complete answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area is written as one definite integral whose integrand is the absolute value of the difference of the two functions, over the interval from the first crossing to the last, and it is evaluated numerically; the bars enclose the whole difference, the returned value matches the sum over the pieces, and BC-ERR-08027 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The single integral form is chosen and the absolute value bars are left off the difference, so the value returned is the signed difference of the lobes, which is BC-ERR-08027; the same underlying state appears as BC-SIG-08010 when the fixed difference is integrated across the crossing.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The absolute value cannot be read as a piecewise definition, so the integrand is not recognised as equal to the piecewise ordered differences, which is BC-PRQ-08003 rather than a formulation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08014 (why the absolute value is what keeps both lobes positive) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08003 (writing the absolute value inside the integrand) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Express the area of a region whose boundary curves cross as a single definite integral of the absolute value of the difference of the two functions, and evaluate it with technology.
skills.description_plain: Use one integral with absolute value bars instead of splitting.
skills.name: Write the area as the integral of the absolute value of the difference

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08016 (the cross sectional dimension read as a function value)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the base is bounded by two curves, so the side is a difference rather than a single value)
adaptive.mastered_if: The side of the cross section at an input is written as the distance between the two boundary curves there, upper minus lower for vertical slices or right minus left for horizontal ones, so both endpoints of the slice appear in the expression; the axis contributes nothing unless it is itself a boundary, and BC-ERR-08028 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The slicing direction is right and the side is taken as the upper function alone, the lower boundary dropped, which is BC-ERR-08028; the volume that follows is then too large by the strip between the lower curve and the axis.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Distance along an axis between two values is not formed as a subtraction, so the side is never a difference, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a cross section gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08016 (that the slice reaches from one boundary curve to the other) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (writing the distance as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a region and an axis of slicing, write the side of the cross section at an input as the difference of the two boundary functions there.
skills.description_plain: Write the side as the top curve minus the bottom curve at that input.
skills.name: Express the side of a cross section as the distance between the curves

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08015 (every volume integral treated as carrying a factor of pi)
BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the named shape is a square, so any pi in the integrand is diagnostic)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as the definite integral of the square of the difference of the boundary functions over the spanning interval, with no factor of pi, and the squared difference is kept as a single squared quantity rather than distributed term by term; neither BC-ERR-08029 nor BC-ERR-08030 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The squared difference integrand is correct and a factor of pi is carried in front of it, which is BC-ERR-08029 and the state in BC-SIG-08011; or the square of the difference is expanded as the difference of the squares, which is BC-ERR-08030 and drops the cross term.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The side of the square was never written as the distance between the curves, so the wrong quantity is squared, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a volume setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08015 (which shape the area formula inside the integral describes) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08031 (writing the side as the difference of the curves) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume of a solid with square cross sections as the definite integral of the square of the difference of the boundary functions over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Square the side and integrate it over the interval.
skills.name: Set up the volume integral for square cross sections

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08016 (the cross sectional dimension read as a function value)
BC-SKL-08032 (square sections, where one dimension does determine the area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the section is a rectangle whose height is stated separately from its base)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as the definite integral of the product of the base and the height of the rectangular section, the base being the distance between the boundary curves and the height being the stated multiple or stated function of that distance, so both dimensions appear as factors; BC-ERR-08031 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The base of the rectangle is written correctly as the difference of the curves and the stated height relation is dropped, so the section is treated as a square, which is BC-ERR-08031.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The base itself is taken as a single function value rather than as a distance between two curves, which is BC-PRQ-08004 and shows before the height relation is reached.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08016 (that a rectangle needs two stated dimensions) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08031 (forming the base as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume of a solid whose rectangular cross sections have a stated height relation as the definite integral of the product of the two dimensions over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Multiply the side by the stated second dimension, then integrate.
skills.name: Set up the volume integral for rectangular cross sections

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as a label for slicing direction)
BC-SKL-08026 (choosing the variable for an area, the same decision in a plane region)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the stem names the axis of perpendicularity, so the variable is dictated rather than chosen)
adaptive.mastered_if: From the phrase naming the axis the cross sections are perpendicular to, the variable of integration is selected, the boundary functions are rewritten in that variable, and the limits are the extent of the base in it; integrand, limits, and differential agree on one variable, and BC-ERR-08023 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The correct variable is named from the phrase and the integrand is left in the other variable, so an expression in x sits under dy or the reverse, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the state in BC-SIG-08009.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary equation cannot be solved for the other variable, so the rewrite is impossible rather than omitted, which is BC-PRQ-08002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (that the differential fixes the variable the integrand must be written in) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (rewriting the boundaries in that variable) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a description of cross sections perpendicular to an axis, select the variable of integration and express the boundary functions in that variable.
skills.description_plain: Read whether the slices stand on the x axis or the y axis and integrate in that variable.
skills.name: Determine the axis the cross sections are perpendicular to

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the integrand is a squared difference, so the cross term is the scored detail)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume integral is evaluated by expanding the squared difference into three terms and antidifferentiating each, or numerically with the unexpanded integrand stored, and the value is reported to the required accuracy; the cross term survives the expansion and no intermediate is truncated, so neither BC-ERR-08030 nor BC-ERR-08005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The setup is correct and the expansion drops the cross term, squaring each part of the difference separately, which is BC-ERR-08030; or the integration is right and a stored decimal is truncated before the last step, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antidifferentiation fails on a term with a negative or fractional exponent produced by the expansion, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a volume gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (that squaring does not distribute over subtraction) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (antidifferentiating the expanded terms) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the volume integral by expanding the squared difference and antidifferentiating, or with technology, and report the value.
skills.description_plain: Expand or use technology, then report the volume.
skills.name: Evaluate a cross section volume integral

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08019 (area formulas recalled without their constant factors)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the named shape is equilateral, so the constant is the whole difference between setups)
adaptive.mastered_if: The area of the equilateral section is written as the square of the distance between the boundary curves multiplied by the square root of three over four, the constant appearing before the integral is assembled, and the distance is a difference of the two curves rather than a single function value; BC-ERR-08032 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The squared distance is correct and the constant is missing or given as one half, so the integrand is the bare square or the general triangle formula, which is BC-ERR-08032.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The area of an equilateral triangle in terms of its side cannot be stated for a numerical side, which is BC-PRQ-08005 rather than a volume setup gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08019 (that each named section carries its own constant) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08005 (the equilateral area formula for a numerical side) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Express the area of an equilateral cross section as the square of the distance between the boundary curves multiplied by the square root of three over four.
skills.description_plain: Use the equilateral triangle formula with the distance as the side.
skills.name: Write the area of an equilateral triangular cross section

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08019 (area formulas recalled without their constant factors)
BC-MIS-08018 (the distance between the curves assumed to be the radius or the leg in every formula)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the stem says which side of the triangle the distance is, so the factor of two is the scored detail)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response reads whether the distance between the curves is a leg or the hypotenuse of the right isosceles section and writes the area as one half the square of that distance in the first case and one quarter of its square in the second, the choice stated rather than assumed; BC-ERR-08033 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The area of a right isosceles triangle is available and the leg formula is applied where the stem makes the distance the hypotenuse, so the integrand is twice the correct one, which is BC-ERR-08033.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The relation between the legs and the hypotenuse of a right isosceles triangle is not available for a numerical case, which is BC-PRQ-08005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08018 (which side of the section the distance between the curves is) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08005 (the two right isosceles area formulas) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Express the area of a right isosceles cross section as half the square of the leg when the distance is a leg, and as one quarter of the square of the hypotenuse when the distance is the hypotenuse.
skills.description_plain: Decide whether the distance is a leg or the hypotenuse, then use the matching formula.
skills.name: Write the area of a right isosceles triangular cross section

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08018 (the distance between the curves treated as the radius)
BC-MIS-08019 (area formulas recalled without their constant factors)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the stem names the distance as the diameter, so the halving appears twice in the correct integrand)
adaptive.mastered_if: With the distance between the boundary curves taken as the diameter, the radius is written as half that distance and the section area as one half of pi times the square of the radius, giving pi over eight times the square of the distance; neither BC-ERR-08034 nor BC-ERR-08035 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The factor of one half for the semicircle is present while the whole distance is used as the radius, which is BC-ERR-08034 and makes the volume four times too large; or the radius is halved correctly and the full circle area is used, which is BC-ERR-08035; BC-SIG-08012 records both integrand forms.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The area of a circle or semicircle of a stated radius cannot be produced, which is BC-PRQ-06007 rather than a diameter gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08018 (diameter against radius) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06007 (the semicircular area formula) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Express the area of a semicircular cross section whose diameter is the distance between the boundary curves as pi over eight times the square of that distance.
skills.description_plain: Halve the distance to get the radius before squaring.
skills.name: Write the area of a semicircular cross section from the diameter

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08019 (area formulas recalled without their constant factors)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08011 (the section shape is named and the volume must be produced end to end)
adaptive.mastered_if: The chosen area formula, complete with its constant, is placed inside a definite integral over the interval the base spans in the slicing variable and evaluated by antidifferentiation or with technology, the value reported as a volume; neither BC-ERR-08032 nor BC-ERR-08030 appears in the assembled integrand.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is assembled over the right interval with the constant of the named section missing, which is BC-ERR-08032; or the squared difference inside it is expanded as a difference of squares, which is BC-ERR-08030.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative of the expanded polynomial integrand is wrong because of exponent handling, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than an assembly gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08019 (carrying the constant of the named section into the integral) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (evaluating the assembled integral) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the definite integral of the chosen area formula over the spanning interval and evaluate it by antidifferentiation or with technology.
skills.description_plain: Put the shape formula in the integral and evaluate it.
skills.name: Set up and evaluate the volume integral for a named cross section

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the region touches the axis, so a single radius carries the whole integrand)
adaptive.mastered_if: For a region touching its axis of revolution, the radius of the disc at an input is written as the distance from the curve to that axis, and it is then squared inside the integrand so that pi multiplies the square rather than the function; BC-ERR-08036 is absent, and the radius reduces to the function value only because the axis is the coordinate axis.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The radius is identified correctly as the distance to the axis and the integrand is pi times the function rather than pi times its square, which is BC-ERR-08036.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Distance from a curve to a line is not formed as a subtraction along the axis, so the radius is never a difference, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (the area of one disc before the integral is written) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (measuring the radius to the axis) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: For a region between a curve and the axis of revolution, write the radius of the disc at an input as the distance from the curve to that axis.
skills.description_plain: The radius is the function value when the axis is the x axis.
skills.name: Identify the radius of a disc as the distance to the axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08015 (a factor of pi attached to every volume)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (revolution about the x axis, where the radius is the function itself)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral with respect to x of the square of the function over the interval the region spans, the constant pi carried through to the reported value; neither BC-ERR-08037 nor BC-ERR-08036 appears, and the squared function is kept as a square rather than distributed.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of the square of the function is correct and the factor pi is dropped from the reported volume, which is BC-ERR-08037 and the state in BC-SIG-08013; or pi is present and the function is not squared, which is BC-ERR-08036.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The radius was never written as the distance from the curve to the axis of revolution, so the wrong quantity is squared, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (the area of a circular slice) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08043 (carrying pi through the evaluation) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume of the solid obtained by revolving the region between a curve and the x axis about the x axis as pi times the definite integral of the square of the function with respect to x.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times the square of the function with respect to x.
skills.name: Set up the disc integral about the x axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08041 (the same disc setup about the x axis)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (revolution about the y axis, so every part of the integral moves to y)
adaptive.mastered_if: The curve is rewritten as a function of y, the volume is written as pi times the definite integral with respect to y of the square of that expression, and the limits are the y values the region spans; integrand, limits, and differential are all in y, so neither BC-ERR-08023 nor BC-ERR-08024 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The structure pi times an integral of a square is correct and the integrand is still a function of x under dy, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the state in BC-SIG-08009; or the expression is rewritten in y and the limits are left as x values, which is BC-ERR-08024.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The equation of the curve cannot be solved for x in terms of y, so the integrand cannot be produced, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a disc method gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (one variable for integrand, limits, and differential) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (solving the curve for x in terms of y) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume of the solid obtained by revolving a region about the y axis as pi times the definite integral, with respect to y, of the square of the curve expressed as a function of y.
skills.description_plain: Rewrite the curve in y, then integrate pi times the square with respect to y.
skills.name: Set up the disc integral about the y axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08020 (a volume of revolution integrating the radius rather than its square)
BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (a numerical volume is requested, so the constant factor shows in the reported value)
adaptive.mastered_if: The disc integral is evaluated by antidifferentiating the squared radius or with technology, and the reported volume retains the factor pi, either as an exact multiple of pi or as a decimal that includes it; unrounded intermediates feed the final step, so neither BC-ERR-08037 nor BC-ERR-08005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral of the square of the radius is evaluated correctly and the answer is reported without pi, which is BC-ERR-08037, the integrand without its constant factor being BC-SIG-08013; or pi is retained and a truncated intermediate moves the value, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The antiderivative of the squared radius is wrong because of exponent handling, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a reporting gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08020 (where pi and the square come from) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (antidifferentiating the squared radius) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Evaluate the disc integral by antidifferentiation or with technology and report the volume, retaining the constant factor of pi.
skills.description_plain: Do the integral and keep pi in the answer.
skills.name: Evaluate a disc volume and report it with the factor of pi

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
BC-MIS-08022 (the limits of integration moved along with the axis)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the axis of revolution is a horizontal line away from the region, so the shift is visible in the radius)
adaptive.mastered_if: For revolution about the horizontal line y equal to k, the radius is written as the function value minus k where the region lies above the line and as k minus the function value where it lies below, so the expression is nonnegative on the interval; the line appears explicitly in the radius, and BC-ERR-08038 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The axis of revolution is correctly identified as a line other than the x axis and the radius in the integrand is the bare function value, which is BC-ERR-08038 and the state observed in BC-SIG-08015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Distance between two values measured along the vertical axis is not formed as a subtraction, so the shift is never written, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius as a distance to the stated axis) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (writing that distance as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: For revolution about the line y equal k, write the radius at an input as the function value minus k when the region lies above the line, and as k minus the function value when it lies below.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the line from the curve, or the curve from the line, whichever is positive.
skills.name: Write the radius as the distance from a curve to a horizontal line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the axis is a vertical line, so the rewrite in y and the shift are both needed)
adaptive.mastered_if: For revolution about the vertical line x equal to h, each boundary is expressed as a function of y and the radius is written as that expression minus h, or h minus it, whichever is nonnegative over the y interval; the line appears in the radius and the differential is dy, so BC-ERR-08038 and BC-ERR-08023 are both absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The curve is rewritten in y and the radius is left as the bare expression with no reference to the line h, which is BC-ERR-08038 and matches BC-SIG-08015; or the shifted radius is correct while the integrand still contains x, which is BC-ERR-08023.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The boundary cannot be solved for x in terms of y, so no expression exists to measure from h, which is BC-PRQ-08002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius as a distance to the stated line) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (expressing the curve in y first) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: For revolution about the line x equal h, write the radius at a y value as the curve expressed in y minus h, or h minus that expression, so that the radius is nonnegative.
skills.description_plain: Use the horizontal distance to the vertical line as the radius.
skills.name: Write the radius as the distance from a curve to a vertical line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08022 (the limits moved along with the axis of revolution)
BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the axis is shifted, so the limits and the radius can fail independently)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted radius over the interval the region spans in the slicing variable, the shift appearing only inside the radius while the limits stay at the extent of the region; neither BC-ERR-08038 nor BC-ERR-08039 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The shifted radius is written correctly and the limits are translated by the same amount as the axis, which is BC-ERR-08039; or the limits are kept and the radius is the unshifted function value, which is BC-ERR-08038 with BC-SIG-08015 as its observed form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distance from the curve to the line is not formed as a difference, so the squared radius is wrong from the start, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08022 (that the translation applies to the radius alone) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08044 (writing the shifted radius) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted radius over the spanning interval, keeping the limits in the variable of slicing.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times the square of the shifted radius.
skills.name: Set up the disc integral about a line other than an axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08022 (the limits moved along with the axis of revolution)
BC-MIS-08012 (limits treated as a viewing window)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08012 (the same region is revolved about a shifted line, so the unchanged limits are the point at issue)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the limits of integration are the extent of the region in the variable of slicing and that moving the axis of revolution changes only the radius, and the same limits are used for revolution about two different lines over the same region; BC-ERR-08039 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The radius is shifted correctly and the interval of integration is translated by the same amount, which is BC-ERR-08039 and leaves a setup that is internally consistent and numerically wrong.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The extent of the region in the slicing variable was never determined, so there is no interval to keep fixed, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08022 (what the limits describe) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08046 (assembling the integral with fixed limits and a shifted radius) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: State that the limits of integration are determined by the extent of the region in the variable of slicing and are unaffected by the position of the axis of revolution.
skills.description_plain: Moving the axis changes the radius, not the interval.
skills.name: Keep the limits of integration unchanged when the axis shifts

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the region is separated from its axis, so both radii exist and can be exchanged)
adaptive.mastered_if: The two boundary curves are compared by their distance from the axis of revolution on the interval, the farther one is assigned the outer radius and the nearer one the inner radius, and the assignment is supported by a value at an interior input; the resulting integrand is nonnegative, and BC-ERR-08040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii are written as distances to the axis and the roles are exchanged, so the integral returns a negative number that is reported or silently made positive, which is BC-ERR-08040 and the observation in BC-SIG-08016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Neither radius is written as a distance to the axis in the first place, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than an assignment gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08023 (that distance from the axis, not height in the plane, assigns the roles) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (measuring each radius to the axis) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a region between two curves and an axis of revolution, determine which curve is farther from the axis on the interval and assign the outer and inner radii accordingly.
