skills.description_plain: The curve farther from the axis gives the outer radius.
skills.name: Identify the outer and inner radii of a washer

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (two radii about the x axis, where squaring order is the scored distinction)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral with respect to x of the square of the outer function minus the square of the inner function, each function squared separately before the subtraction, over the interval the region spans; neither BC-ERR-08030 nor BC-ERR-08037 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The outer and inner curves are assigned correctly and the integrand is pi times the square of their difference, which is BC-ERR-08030 and the not mastered form in BC-SIG-08014; or the difference of squares is right and the factor pi is dropped, which is BC-ERR-08037.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The two radii were never written as distances to the axis, so the squares are of the wrong quantities, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (the ring area as a difference of two disc areas) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08048 (assigning outer and inner before squaring) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume as pi times the definite integral, with respect to x, of the square of the outer function minus the square of the inner function over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times outer squared minus inner squared with respect to x.
skills.name: Set up the washer integral about the x axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
BC-SKL-08049 (the same washer setup about the x axis)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (revolution about the y axis, so both radii and the limits move to y)
adaptive.mastered_if: Both boundaries are expressed as functions of y, the volume is written as pi times the definite integral with respect to y of the square of the right boundary minus the square of the left boundary, and the limits are the y values the region spans; neither BC-ERR-08023 nor BC-ERR-08024 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The washer structure is right and one or both expressions in the integrand remain in x under dy, which is BC-ERR-08023 and the state in BC-SIG-08009; or the integrand is fully in y with x values as limits, which is BC-ERR-08024.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Solving either boundary equation for x in terms of y does not go through, which is BC-PRQ-08002 rather than a washer gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08013 (matching integrand, limits, and differential) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (rewriting both boundaries in y) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume as pi times the definite integral, with respect to y, of the square of the right boundary minus the square of the left boundary over the interval of y values.
skills.description_plain: Rewrite both curves in y, then integrate the difference of squares.
skills.name: Set up the washer integral about the y axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the ring area is the entire content of the integrand, so the two forms are directly comparable)
adaptive.mastered_if: The response states that the ring area is pi times the outer radius squared minus pi times the inner radius squared and uses that form, and it can show with two numerical radii that this differs from pi times the square of their difference by the cross term; BC-ERR-08030 is absent wherever a washer integrand is written.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The washer is described correctly in words as a disc with a hole and the integrand written is still the square of the difference of the radii, which is BC-ERR-08030 and the not mastered observation in BC-SIG-08014.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Expanding the square of a binomial loses the cross term, so the two expressions look identical algebraically, which is BC-PRQ-06002 rather than a washer gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (the ring as the difference of two disc areas) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-06002 (expanding a squared binomial correctly) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: State and use the fact that the ring area is pi times the outer radius squared minus pi times the inner radius squared, which is not pi times the square of the difference of the radii.
skills.description_plain: Square each radius first, then subtract.
skills.name: Subtract the squares of the radii rather than squaring their difference

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (two radii and a shifted horizontal axis, so shift and assignment can fail separately)
adaptive.mastered_if: For revolution about y equal to k, the outer radius is written as the distance from the farther curve to the line and the inner radius as the distance from the nearer curve to the line, each as a difference containing k and each nonnegative on the interval; neither BC-ERR-08038 nor BC-ERR-08040 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii are shifted by k and the roles are exchanged, which is BC-ERR-08040 with the negative value recorded in BC-SIG-08016; or the roles are right and the radii are written as bare function values with no k, which is BC-ERR-08038 and BC-SIG-08015.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distance from a curve to a horizontal line is not formed as a subtraction, which is BC-PRQ-08004 rather than a washer gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08021 (radii as distances to the stated line) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08004 (writing each distance as a difference) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: For revolution about y equal k, write the outer radius as the distance from the farther curve to the line and the inner radius as the distance from the nearer curve to the line.
skills.description_plain: Subtract the line value from each curve before squaring.
skills.name: Write both washer radii as distances from a horizontal line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
BC-MIS-08013 (the differential treated as changeable without changing the integrand)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (a vertical axis away from the region, so the rewrite in y and the shift are both required)
adaptive.mastered_if: For revolution about x equal to h, both boundary curves are written as functions of y and each radius is the distance from that curve to h, so the integrand contains h and no x and the differential is dy; neither BC-ERR-08023 nor BC-ERR-08038 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The curves are rewritten in y and the radii carry no reference to h, which is BC-ERR-08038 and the state in BC-SIG-08015; or the shift to h is applied while one expression is still in x, which is BC-ERR-08023.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: Solving the boundary equations for x in terms of y fails, so there is nothing to measure from the line, which is BC-PRQ-08002.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08021 (radii measured to the stated vertical line) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08002 (expressing both curves in y) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: For revolution about x equal h, express both boundary curves as functions of y and write each radius as the distance from that curve to the line h.
skills.description_plain: Use horizontal distances from the vertical line for both curves.
skills.name: Write both washer radii as distances from a vertical line

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08023 (the upper curve assumed to give the outer radius)
BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (the axis lies above the region, so position and distance disagree)
adaptive.mastered_if: The distances from both boundary curves to the axis of revolution are compared on the interval, and the farther curve is named the outer radius even when the axis lies above the region and the upper curve is the nearer one; the comparison is supported at an interior input, and BC-ERR-08040 is absent.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both distances are written correctly and the outer role is given to the upper curve by position in the plane rather than by distance, which is BC-ERR-08040 and produces the negative integrand observed in BC-SIG-08016.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distance from each curve to the axis is not expressed as a difference, so no comparison is possible, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08023 (that the axis, not the plane, decides outer and inner) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08052 (writing both radii as distances before comparing) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Compare the distances from each boundary curve to the axis of revolution on the interval to assign the outer and inner radii, noting that revolving about a line above the region reverses the roles.
skills.description_plain: Check which curve is farther from the line, which can differ from which is higher.
skills.name: Determine which boundary curve is farther from the shifted axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08017 (the difference of squares equated to the square of the difference)
BC-MIS-08021 (the radius taken as the function value whatever the axis is)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08013 (a shifted axis with two radii, where the shift and the squaring order are independent)
adaptive.mastered_if: The volume is written as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted outer radius minus the square of the shifted inner radius, each radius containing the line of revolution and each squared before the subtraction, over the unshifted interval; neither BC-ERR-08030 nor BC-ERR-08038 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: Both radii carry the shift and the integrand is the square of their difference, which is BC-ERR-08030 and BC-SIG-08014; or the difference of squares is correct and the radii are the bare function values, which is BC-ERR-08038 with BC-SIG-08015 as its form.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The distances to the axis are not formed as differences, so both squares are of the wrong quantities, which is BC-PRQ-08004.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08017 (the ring area as a difference of two disc areas) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08052 (writing both shifted radii) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Write the volume as pi times the definite integral of the square of the shifted outer radius minus the square of the shifted inner radius over the spanning interval.
skills.description_plain: Integrate pi times the difference of the squares of the two shifted radii.
skills.name: Set up the washer integral about a line other than an axis

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-SKL-09011 (the parametric length integral, which combines two derivatives)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (the arc length integral must be stated, so the integrand form is the whole answer)
adaptive.mastered_if: The length of the graph of f on [a,b] is stated as the definite integral of the square root of one plus the square of f prime with respect to x, the added one inside the radical and the derivative squared under it, with the limits taken from the interval; BC-ERR-08041 is absent, and the expression is named as a length rather than an area.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: An integral over the correct interval is written with the radical present and the added one missing, or with the derivative under the radical but not squared, which is BC-ERR-08041 in its two recorded forms.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The magnitude of a two component quantity is not formed by the Pythagorean relation, so the radical is not reconstructed, which is BC-PRQ-08007 rather than an arc length gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (what the radical integrand measures) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08007 (the Pythagorean magnitude the integrand comes from) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a differentiable function and an interval, write the definite integral of the square root of one plus the square of the derivative over that interval as the length of the curve.
skills.description_plain: Write the integral of the square root of one plus the derivative squared.
skills.name: State the arc length integral for a function on an interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-SKL-08056 (stating the general formula rather than instantiating it)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (a specific function on a specific interval, so the substitution and the limits are both visible)
adaptive.mastered_if: The given function is differentiated, the derivative is squared and placed under the radical with the added one, and the limits are the endpoints of the interval described in the stem; the derivative is squared as a whole, and neither BC-ERR-08042 nor BC-ERR-08019 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The derivative is computed correctly and substituted under the radical without being squared, which is BC-ERR-08042; or the integrand is assembled correctly while the limits come from inputs other than the described interval, which is BC-ERR-08019.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The derivative itself is wrong, or the function is not differentiable at a point inside the interval and that is not noticed, which is BC-SKL-02021 and evaluation by antidifferentiation is BC-SKL-06034; misreading the interval from the stem is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (what the assembled integral measures) for the conceptual case; BC-SKL-08056 (the integrand the substitution feeds) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Differentiate the given function, substitute the derivative into the arc length integrand, and attach the limits taken from the described interval.
skills.description_plain: Differentiate the given function and place it inside the radical.
skills.name: Set up an arc length integral from a described curve

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
BC-MIS-08009 (an interpretation treated as complete once the quantity is named)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (the integral is displayed and only its identification is scored, so interval and object separate cleanly)
adaptive.mastered_if: A displayed integral of the square root of one plus a squared derivative is named as the length of the graph of that function, and the interval is stated as running between the two limits of integration; both the object and the interval appear in the sentence, and neither BC-ERR-08043 nor BC-ERR-08044 is present.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: The integral is named as the length of the curve with no interval given, which is BC-ERR-08043 and the observation in BC-SIG-08017; or the radical integral is described as the area under the graph, which is BC-ERR-08044.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The function whose derivative sits inside the radical cannot be identified from the notation, so the sentence has no subject, which is BC-PRQ-06005.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08024 (a radical integrand against an area integrand) for the conceptual case; BC-ERR-08043 (naming the interval alongside the object) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Given a definite integral of the square root of one plus a squared derivative, state that it is the length of the graph of the function on the interval given by the limits.
skills.description_plain: Recognise the radical form and say which curve and interval it measures.
skills.name: Identify a given integral as an arc length and name the interval

common_confusions: BC-MIS-08003 (a calculator value treated as standing on its own)
BC-MIS-08024 (every definite integral read as an area)
diagnostic_archetypes: BC-QA-08014 (the integrand has no elementary antiderivative, so the written expression is the only record of method)
adaptive.mastered_if: The arc length integral is written on the page with its radical integrand and limits, evaluated numerically, and reported to three places after the decimal point from unrounded stored values; neither BC-ERR-08045 nor BC-ERR-08005 appears.
adaptive.partially_mastered_if: A correct decimal length appears with no integral expression anywhere, which is BC-ERR-08045; or the setup is shown and a truncated intermediate derivative or bound is reused, moving the third decimal place, which is BC-ERR-08005.
adaptive.prerequisite_gap_if: The value is right but rounded to the wrong number of places or rounded against the stated convention, which is BC-PRQ-08006 rather than an evaluation gap.
adaptive.remediation_target: BC-MIS-08003 (the written integral as the scored object) for the conceptual case; BC-PRQ-08006 (three place reporting from stored values) for the procedural case.

skills.description_formal: Evaluate an arc length integral numerically and report the value accurate to three places after the decimal point.
skills.description_plain: Enter the radical integrand and report the decimal.
skills.name: Evaluate an arc length integral with technology
